name: social-flow
description: Channel-based short-form and long-form content pipeline. Pick the format when you start a storyboard — 9:16 shorts for Threads, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, or 16:9 YouTube long-form with chapters — then author the storyboard under data/[channel]/episodes/[topic]/, produce the video and the per-platform text, and publish it after a HITL approval gate. Long-form episodes mix clips you film yourself with generated scenes, and scenes that need words or diagrams on screen become HTML slides — planned in the storyboard, authored only after approval; a slide that states a value becomes a motion slide (count-ups, growing bars, steps entering on their sentence), rendered locally frame by frame at no cost and admitted to the build only after an adversarial design review scores it 95 or higher. Narration defaults to your own voice on every scene, so the shooting script carries the lines for every shot: filmed shots get screen, action, lines and a filename, the rest are voice-only recordings. Research writes three scenario candidates and loops each to 95 on curiosity, fear, intrigue and comedy before you pick. After that, six board reads run once each — copy, every scene, word choice, the camera plan (what each shot should make the audience feel, and the size, angle, frame space and move that serve it), the sound plan, and the generated images. Those six have no score to clear: findings get applied once, and anything left over goes onto the approval screen. The autoproduce skill runs the same path unattended, replacing the approval gate with the machine gates and an economy tier. Per-platform setup and growth skills open the accounts and then run autonomous growth loops. A built-in MCP server ships 61 tools (52 without credentials) — publishing, insights, search, open data, and image, video, voice and music generation — with no external MCP dependency.
